rules: Execute one batch at a time in the declared order.
Do not start the next batch until the current batch has implementation, tests, audit, documentation, evidence, and exit-gate approval.
A passing test is evidence for only the behavior and environment it actually exercised.
Absence of a defect report is not evidence of correctness.
The exact release artifact, not a mutable source checkout, is the final qualification subject.

allowed_changes: Fix a verified defect in locked scope.
Complete, simplify, or remove a capability already required by a locked workflow.
Add tests, observability, documentation, packaging, security, migration, recovery, or release infrastructure required by an active batch.
Replace a mock, demo, placeholder, alias, or unsafe fallback with a truthful implementation or an explicit unavailable state.
Make a minimal enabling change that is necessary to close a current batch and record that necessity in batch evidence.
prohibited_changes: Add a new end-user capability outside the locked personal-core workflows.
Expand platform promises beyond qualified Windows 11 x64 behavior.
Add aliases or presentation surfaces to inflate capability or tool counts.
Activate E01 or later expansion work.
Claim production readiness, stability, privacy, offline behavior, security, or success without the required evidence.
exception_process: Record the requested change and the locked workflow or exit gate it enables.
Prove that deferring it prevents the current batch from closing.
Add tests and documentation in the same batch.
Update capabilities.json, scorecard.json, and batch evidence when the capability, lifecycle, implementation reality, or score changes.

locked_until: B15 completes a 30-consecutive-day dogfood qualification with all thresholds met.
B16 qualifies the exact distributable artifacts and closes every release gate.
The release artifact is frozen and its evidence bundle is immutable.
rules: Evaluate one expansion independently against owner value, maintenance cost, privacy, risk, and fit with the core promise.
A new feature starts experimental; it cannot inherit stable status from the core release.
Every expansion must define availability, result states, consent, timeouts, cancellation, verification, tests, documentation, telemetry boundaries, and removal policy before promotion.
Expansion failure must not regress a qualified core workflow.
Commercial validation remains a separate optional track and cannot retroactively inflate the personal-core score.

stable_claim_requirements: All capability and workflow qualification checks pass on the primary platform.
No mock, demo, placeholder, stub, canned response, or unverified fallback can reach the stable path.
The release evidence identifies the exact artifact, environment, test command, timestamp, and result.
A non-empty owner, entry point, complete dependency/model/account/hardware audit, and verified platform are recorded.
Required unit/contract, integration, end-to-end, and applicable hardware test evidence is mapped and release-qualified.
Every claimed stable tool action and API endpoint has per-interface evidence of a real implementation.
Every network-capable stable feature has a current release-qualified privacy disclosure and destination inventory.
forbidden_claim_patterns: A fallback that did not perform the requested effect reports success.
An optional integration is described as included or working when it is unconfigured.
A test count is presented without a command, environment, and current result.
Offline or local-only behavior is claimed without an enforced no-egress check.
A capability count includes aliases, demos, mocks, removed features, or unavailable integrations as working tools.
